archetypes.name: kv-contract
archetypes.rationale: The plan defines a precise result-env allowlist for each driver and ROUTE enum consumed by the orchestrator; mismatches between the .md contract, phase_driver_write_result_env calls, and orchestrator branching are the plan's own stated #1 failure mode.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit the KV contract between each new phase driver and the SKILL.md orchestrator: verify that every key the plan lists in the result-env allowlist for design-route.sh (ROUTE, BRAINSTORM_PREFIX, ERROR, WARN, RESUME_STEP, SESSION_ID, RUN_ID, TIER, BRAINSTORM_DONE, and the cancel-route keys) and design-init-runparams.sh (INIT_STATUS, RENAMED, RUN_PARAMS_PATH, DESIGN_CLASSIFICATION, WARN) is both written by the driver and read or branched on by the orchestrator in the SKILL.md update plan. Check that the ROUTE enum {proceed, cancel-title-filter, cancel-reentry-guard, resume@<STEP>, clarify, already-planned} in design-route.md and the SKILL.md ROUTE switch arms are exhaustive and aligned with no unhandled value. Verify that BRAINSTORM_PREFIX pre-branch handling is precisely ordered: the plan states it must be applied after reading the result env but before the ROUTE branch, not inside individual branch arms — check the SKILL.md update plan preserves this. Confirm that ERROR from LOAD_OK=false fallthrough is in the design-route allowlist and that the orchestrator re-emits it as a warning breadcrumb on the normal-path continuation, not silently discarded. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: harness-repoint
archetypes.rationale: The plan ships no new test harnesses and relies entirely on re-pointing existing test-design-structure.sh and test-step0b-router-flag-recovery.sh assertions; gaps leave failure modes without a CI-visible detection path, which is the plan's own stated #2 failure mode.
archetypes.prompt_body: For each of the plan's four listed failure modes (KV-contract drift, harness under-update, routing-order regression, non-executable drivers), determine whether the re-pointed test-design-structure.sh assertions described in the plan would actually catch a regression — specifically, check that greps re-pointed to design-route.sh and design-init-runparams.sh target content that will exist in those scripts as described, and that the routing-order check (Check 24) verifies title-filter precedes reentry-guard precedes clarify within the driver, not just in the orchestrator. Verify that the test-step0b-router-flag-recovery.sh update described in the plan preserves all 7 merge-case test behaviors unchanged and only redirects header and comment anchors to the driver file. Assess whether the plan's 'manual smoke' and 'probe external tool invocations' testing steps are specific enough to be actionable — i.e., do they name concrete commands and expected outputs, or do they leave pass/fail ambiguous. Check whether the plan's testing strategy covers the env-before-rename ordering invariant and the LOAD_OK=false fallthrough path with a CI-detectable assertion. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
